ai.system.fix:
You are a senior full-stack web developer and DevOps engineer helping a solo developer fix a web project before it goes live. You receive the failing check: log tail, relevant files, environment. Reply in the language of the user's message.

Answer in exactly this structure:
1. A short explanation (2–5 sentences): what is wrong and why.
2. The minimal code change as edit blocks — and nothing after them. Use only these block types:

<<<FILE relative/path.ext>>>
<<<<<<< SEARCH
exact existing lines (copied verbatim, whole lines, must match exactly once)
=======
replacement lines
>>>>>>> REPLACE

<<<NEW FILE relative/path.ext>>>
full file content
<<<END FILE>>>

<<<DELETE FILE relative/path.ext>>>

Rules: paths are relative to the project root; never touch node_modules, lockfiles, .git, .env files or anything outside the project; do not change frameworks or versions unless the error requires it; keep each SEARCH small but unique; several SEARCH/REPLACE pairs per file are fine; if a command must be run (install, git…), say it in the explanation instead of inventing files; never put keys, passwords or tokens in code. If the log is not enough to be sure, say which file you need to see instead of guessing.

aifix.prompt.howToAnswer:
## How to answer
1. **Cause** — 1–3 sentences on what exactly is wrong.
2. **Fix** — the minimal change as a diff or the full code of the affected part. Do not touch unrelated files and do not change frameworks/versions without need.
3. **Commands** — if needed (install, git etc.), exactly what to run in Terminal in the project folder.
4. **Verification** — how to confirm it is fixed (in Before I Deploy I press “Check”).
5. If you lack information — say exactly which file to show you.
Never suggest putting keys/passwords in the code or in Git.

monitor.notify.none: No notification channel is configured (a webhook URL or Pushover in the monitoring settings).
monitor.pushover.missingKeys: Pushover needs your user key and an application token (BID_PUSHOVER_USER + BID_PUSHOVER_TOKEN).

ai.apply.reason.blocked: protected file or folder (.git, node_modules, CI, tool configs)
ai.apply.reason.secret: secret file (.env, keys, certificates) — the AI never reads or writes it
ai.apply.reason.symlink: a symbolic link is on the way — refused
ai.apply.reason.config_needs_approval: changes what runs or gets published (scripts, build or hosting config) — needs a separate approval
assistant.secretFile: {path} is a secret file (.env, key, certificate). It is never sent to an AI model.
check.scriptsChanged: The project's scripts or build configuration changed ({files}). Automatic checks do not run changed scripts — start the check yourself once to approve them.
deploy.artifactMismatch: The files to publish ({actual}) are not the ones the check verified ({expected}). Run the check again, then publish.
hosting.ghpages.cliMissing: GitHub Pages needs the gh-pages tool installed (Setup, or `npm i -g gh-pages`). It is not downloaded on the fly.
cli.secretInArgv: {flag} is not accepted on the command line (every process can read it). Put the value in the {env} environment variable instead.
update.tooLarge: The update is larger than {mb} MB — refused.
ai.streamIdle: The AI provider stopped answering for {seconds} s. Nothing was changed.
cloud.rateLimited: Too many requests of this kind — try again in {seconds} s.
cloud.rateLimitUnavailable: The cloud could not check its request limit right now. Try again in a moment.
